newsitem.title: INDIA: India's IndusInd Bank to make equity issue in '97.
newsitem.headline: India's IndusInd Bank to make equity issue in '97.

text.p: India's private sector IndusInd Bank will make a public issue of equity in August-September this year, a bank official said on Thursday.
"We would like to go public in the months of August and September this year," S. Solomon Raj, managing director of the bank, told Reuters.
"The size of the issue is likely to be 450 million rupees," Raj said. "The premium will depend on how many times the earnings per share should be discounted."
"We would like to go to the public with a premium of 40 rupees (per share) because we got a premium of 40 rupees from the promoting companies for the previous shares," he said.
Raj said the bank was also considering a 100 million rupee preferential issue of shares to the shareholders of the promoting companies. This would be before the public issue, he said.
The two promoter firms are IndusInd Enterprises and Finance Ltd., and IndusInd International (Mauritius) Holdings Ltd.

Raj said IndusInd Bank's net profit rose 61 percent to 733.2 million rupees for the year ending March 31, 1997, as compared to 456.2 million the previous year. This translates into an earnings per share of 6.11 rupees, as compared to 3.89 the previous year.

IndusInd Bank had deposits of 3,093.1 million rupees and advances of 1,927.7 million in financial year 1996/97 (April-March), against 1,412.2 million and 1,121.2 million respectively the previous year.
